summary: Oak Park sits in the eastern Conejo Valley of Ventura County, tucked against the Santa Monica Mountains, and its 5.3 square miles pack a geographic punch that belies the modest population of roughly 13,600 — step outside and the terrain rolls into oak-studded hillsides and canyon edges that frame sunsets dropping behind the Conejo Grade to the west. The median home price tops a million dollars, yet with a median household income around $160,000, the price-to-income ratio lands near 6.3:1 — expensive by national standards but noticeably less stretched than neighboring parts of western Los Angeles County, which partly explains the commute dynamic: Oak Park functions largely as a bedroom community, with the 101 freeway funneling workers toward Thousand Oaks, Westlake Village, and the longer slog into the San Fernando Valley. Annual daytime highs average 75°F with nearly ten hours of daily sunshine, though summer afternoons in this inland valley can push well past 90°F before the marine layer creeps through the Conejo Pass and drops nighttime temps to a comfortable mid-50s. The landscape rewards evening walks — open-space preserves and trail networks threading the surrounding hills connect to broader Santa Monica Mountains paths. With a 3.3% poverty rate and a rent median above $3,100, the economic bandwidth here is narrow, and the retail and dining scene reflects that compression: functional rather than destination-worthy, leaning on nearby Thousand Oaks for variety. Oak Park is essentially a well-maintained pocket of Ventura County suburbia where the geography outperforms the nightlife by a wide margin.
